Bread Glossary

Fresh from the oven, user_name. Tap a term for the details.

Hydration

Water as a percentage of flour weight. 75% hydration means 750g water per 1kg flour. Higher hydration means a more open, holey crumb.

Autolyse

Resting flour and water before adding salt or yeast, letting gluten form on its own. Twenty minutes does a lot of quiet work.

Bulk Ferment

The first rise, from mixing to shaping. This is where flavour is built. Rushing it is the classic beginner's mistake.

Proof

The second rise, usually in the shaped loaf. Under-proofed dough springs back fast when poked; over-proofed dough leaves a dent.

Levain / Starter

A flour-and-water culture of wild yeast and bacteria. Feed it, and it rewards you with lift and tang.

Crumb

The inside structure of the loaf. Not the same as crumbs on your counter, though those happen too.

Baker's Percentage

A system where flour is always 100% and everything else is measured against it. Makes scaling a recipe painless.

Chess Endgame Glossary

Fewer pieces, sharper ideas, user_name.

Zugzwang

German for "compulsion to move." Every move you make worsens your position, but pass is not allowed. Cruel and elegant.

Opposition

When kings face each other with one square between them. Whoever must move loses the standoff—a king-and-pawn endgame essential.

Promotion

A pawn reaching the last rank becomes any piece, almost always a queen. "Underpromotion" to a knight is rare and glorious.

Lucena Position

A classic rook-and-pawn winning setup. Learn it once and you'll spot it for life.

Fortress

A drawn setup where the weaker side walls up so completely that the extra material can't break through.

Fifty-Move Rule

If fifty moves pass with no capture and no pawn move, either player may claim a draw. Memory aid for long grinds.

Triangulation

A king manoeuvre that wastes a tempo to hand the opponent the zugzwang. Sneaky, satisfying, worth practising.

Greenware

Unfired clay that's bone-dry and ready for the kiln. Handle it like it owes you money—because it cracks easily.

instances.html:
Fishing Glossary

Cast, wait, learn a word, user_name.

Bait vs Lure

Bait is something a fish eats (worms, chunk bait). A lure is a fake that triggers a strike reaction. Different psychology, same rod.

Leader

A short length of clear or heavier line between your main line and the hook. Adds stealth and abrasion resistance.

Drag

The reel's tension setting. Too loose and a big fish runs; too tight and the line snaps. Set it by feel, not by hope.

Noodle Rod

A very flexible rod, often used for light line and big fish. Bends almost double so the line doesn't break.

Backing

Extra line behind the fly line on a reel. Buys you room when a fish decides to head for the far bank.

Home Networking Glossary

For when the internet "just stops," user_name.

The modem translates your provider's signal. The router shares that connection across your devices. Sometimes one box does both.

DHCP

The service that hands out IP addresses automatically. If it fails, devices show a 169.254 address and nothing works.

DNS

The phonebook that turns names like example.com into numeric addresses. Slow DNS feels like slow internet.

The network's name. Don't name it something embarrassing, because your neighbours can see it.

The exposure triangle and beyond.

    The size of the lens opening. Measured in f-stops (e.g., f/2.8, f/16). Lower f-number = wider opening = more light and shallower depth of field.

    Adjusts colors so whites look white under different lighting. Auto usually works; presets (daylight, cloudy, tungsten) give more control.

  • Fartlek — Swedish for "speed play." Unstructured surges.
  • Negative split — second half faster than the first. Chef's kiss.
  • Cadence — steps per minute. ~170–180 is a common target.
  • VO₂ max — how much oxygen you can actually use. Trainable, slowly.
  • Taper — cutting volume before a race so you arrive fresh.
  • Bonk — glycogen's empty and the wall is real.

Chess Knight & Bishop Endgame Glossary

  • Wrong bishop — it doesn't control your pawn's promotion square. Draw.
  • Opposite-coloured bishops — drawish, even a pawn down.
  • Good bishop — outside your own pawn chain, free to roam.
  • Knight on the rim — dim. Centralised knights dominate.
  • Fortress — a setup that holds forever despite being down material.
  • Zugzwang — every move makes it worse. You must move anyway.
  • Domination — the enemy piece has squares, none of them safe.

Woodworking Glossary

Measure twice, curse once, user_name.

Terms worth knowing
  • Dado — a flat groove cut across the grain.
  • Rabbet — an L-shaped step along an edge.
  • Board foot — 1" × 12" × 12". How lumber is sold.
  • Kiln dried — moisture cooked down to ~6–8%. Stable.
  • Grain direction — plane with it, or tear out and learn.
  • Cupping — a board bowing across its width as it dries.
  • Kerf — the width your blade removes. Account for it.
  • Figure — the pretty pattern: quilt, curl, birdseye.
